items.t: I was thinking a bit about the Pokemon League, and how it felt a little odd that so many people - really everyone - in the Plateau is some kind of “outsider” trying to undermine or reform the governments or cultures of their regions, like surely someone there would’ve been a “by the book” cog-in-the-machine sort of person who’d be more part of the problems than the solutions… But then it also kinda clicked (and idk if this was intentional or if it really just emerged naturally) that like of course the Pokemon League would be the place where the exception to this tendency happens. In a society driven so much by bloodlines and traditionalism, outsiders or reformers to those systems would naturally find a home in the one place where influence and power are granted on a more meritocratic basis. The people interested in preserving the structures of power are more likely than not already a part of them, they wouldn’t need the League with the same level of need that drives the others to it. And then the rest follows from there - it’s a “gap” in the system for outsiders to make their mark. Kender uses that to his personal advantage, to pull one (well, to pull a lot) over on a society that wouldn’t normally give him the time of day, Lance uses it to try and force the system to be as noble as it’s supposed to be (and obviously to provide a haven for the next generation of champions), and Leaf takes that principle and runs with it even further (taking advantage of the public goodwill Lance brought back to the league after Kender). And each champion favors the same traits in their Elite Four, maintaining the Plateau as a sort of political outlier in the region. It all flows naturally. I really appreciate that about your writing - it’s clear you put a lot of thought into “What kind of people, cultures, or circumstances leads to this situation not being a contrivance, but an inevitability?” Even if you didn’t exactly plan all of this political domino effect, it’s the sort of thing that crops up naturally when everything else around it is clicking together so well.
